decision.summary: Jonah Okafor (P-202) asked on the portal for an update on his boiler job and about bin collection. I emailed him (his preferred channel) the status of R-4799: the £780 first quote is with the landlord, who asked for a second quote, with Swift P&H visiting on 14 October 2026; a decision is pending. I told him the bin collection is a council matter (London Borough of Tower Hamlets) and raised no new ticket.

answers.question: What is the current status of his boiler job and what does it mean for him?
answers.answer: R-4799 (routine heating, boiler pressure dropping) is at double_quotation. A £780 quote for expansion vessel replacement was received on 2026-10-03. The landlord asked for a second quote, and Swift P&H is booked to visit on 2026-10-14. Nothing is approved yet, so the repair has not started. For him: the boiler is still losing pressure and needs weekly top-ups, and the target is to resolve it within 14 days (routine). He should report any loss of heating or hot water straight away, as that would be an emergency.

answers.question: How do you handle the bin question?
answers.answer: Not a landlord or agency repair. Waste collection is run by the council (London Borough of Tower Hamlets), so I told him to contact the council about the missed collection. I did not give a collection date because none is on record.

answers.question: Do you create any new tickets?
answers.answer: No. The boiler issue already has an open ticket (R-4799), so a new one would be a duplicate. The bin issue is for the council, so no agency ticket is needed.

actions_claimed.description: Emailed Jonah Okafor (MSG-101) with boiler status, Swift P&H visit on 14 Oct, and council advice for bin collection.
Added internal note NOTE-102 to R-4799 recording the enquiry and reply.

conflicts: The portal chat came from the tenant's portal session. No identity check tool was available, so I sent the reply to the email address on the CRM record and gave only general ticket status, not cost or landlord detail. The £780 quote amount was left out of the tenant message.
assumptions: Boiler is still working (only pressure loss), so this is routine, not an emergency. Tenant has no mention of heating or hot water loss.
The 'Swift P&H visit 2026-10-14' note is taken as a confirmed booking.
Tenant is entitled to status updates on his own ticket; his preferred channel is email.

args.body:
Hi Jonah,

Thanks for getting in touch, and sorry it has felt slow.

Your boiler job (reference R-4799) is about the boiler losing pressure, so it needs topping up each week. The original repair quote has been received, but your landlord has asked us to get a second quote before going ahead. A second contractor, Swift P&H, is booked to visit on 14 October 2026. Once we have both quotes, the landlord will decide how to proceed, and we will let you know as soon as there is an update. This is a routine repair, so the target is to have it sorted within 14 days.

In the meantime, please keep an eye on the boiler pressure gauge and top up as you normally would. If the boiler stops working altogether, or you have no heating or hot water, please tell us straight away by replying here. If you smell gas, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

On bin collection: we don't manage waste collection, so this one is for your council. Please contact London Borough of Tower Hamlets about the missed collection. They can tell you when it will be collected.

Best wishes,
Property Management Team
